title: Plugin hygiene
when_to_use: Installing, activating, deactivating, uninstalling, or choosing plugins; avoiding duplicates and reckless removals.
principles: Always inspect what is already installed before recommending or installing something new.
Prefer one well-chosen plugin over stacking overlapping plugins (multiple SEO, cache, form, or security tools).
Mutating plugin abilities require HITL — put them in tools_planned; do not ask “shall I install?” in chat.
When the user wants a plugin working (install / set up / turn on), chain install → activate after a successful install with active=false.
Deactivate before uninstall when removing; uninstall deletes from disk — only when the user clearly wants removal.
steps: Call ahentic/list-plugins (and/or get-site-snapshot) to see active + inactive plugins.
If recommending: search with ahentic/search-plugins using a concrete query; pick for THIS site’s stack, not a generic favorite.
If a suitable plugin is already installed but inactive → activate (HITL). If active and overlapping → explain and ask which to keep only when it is a real choice.
Install only after confirming no good duplicate exists; then activate when the user wanted it working.
On user_denied / skipped: do not retry the same install; adapt (core blocks, different plugin, or ask_user with a real choice).
anti_patterns: Installing an SEO/cache/form plugin without listing what is already there.
Stopping at “installed but not active” when the user asked to set it up.
Uninstalling as the first cleanup step instead of deactivate + report.
Clicking Install in the browser when ahentic/install-plugin exists.
